alert.title: High p99 latency on orders-api
alert.description: p99 latency rose from 140ms to 3.1s within 2 minutes of deploying v5.2.0. DB connection pool utilisation is steady at 35% with no pool-wait warnings. Profiling shows a new synchronous call to recommendations-api on every request; recommendations-api itself is healthy at its usual 400ms p99.

notes: Latency title with the DB pool explicitly ruled out. The regression is a blocking call added in the deploy; the dependency itself is healthy, so not dependency_failure.

alert.title: CrashLoopBackOff on payments-api
alert.description: Pods restart every ~40s. Last state: Terminated, reason OOMKilled, exit code 137. Memory limit 512Mi; the heap grows past it while the in-memory cache warms up at startup.

notes: Looks like a crash loop, but the termination reason is OOMKilled. Memory is the mechanism; startup_crash is accepted because it happens during warm-up.

alert.title: Elevated 5xx error rate on checkout-api
alert.description: 5xx rate at 18% (baseline 0.3%). All errors are 503s returned from calls to payments-api. checkout-api has not been deployed in 6 days, and payments-api's status page reports a partial outage.

notes: Same title as the generated bad-deploy scenario, but there is no deploy and the errors come from a failing upstream.

alert.title: Disk usage high on search-api node
alert.description: Root volume at 94% and rising about 2% every 10 minutes since yesterday's release v8.1, which set LOG_LEVEL=debug. /var/log/search-api is 41GB. Log rotation is configured but rotates daily.

notes: The disk filling is the mechanism; the debug-logging release is the trigger, so bad_deploy is also accepted.

alert.title: Intermittent TLS handshake failures on api-gateway
alert.description: About 30% of client requests fail with 'x509: certificate has expired'. Certificate renewal succeeded 3 days ago, but 2 of 6 load-balancer nodes still serve the old certificate.

notes: Renewal looks fine at first glance; the new certificate was not rolled out everywhere.

alert.title: Request timeouts on user-service
alert.description: Requests time out after 30s and logs are full of 'timed out waiting for connection from pool'. Postgres shows 180 sessions from user-service idle in transaction since the 09:10 deploy.

expected_runbook: High p99 latency / database connection pool saturation
notes: Timeouts rather than a latency title. A connection leak shipped in a deploy exhausts the pool; bad_deploy is also accepted.

alert.title: Pods not becoming ready on inventory-service
alert.description: New pods exit with code 1 about 2s after start with 'KeyError: INVENTORY_DB_URL'. The variable was removed from the config map in this morning's change.

notes: A crash at startup caused by a config change; bad_deploy is also accepted.

alert.title: Latency increase on cart-service
alert.description: p95 latency 1.8s (baseline 120ms). RSS on every pod has grown from 600Mi to 1.9Gi over 3 days without restarts, and GC pause time is up 12x. No deploys this week; DB metrics normal.

notes: A latency title, but the signals point to a memory leak causing GC thrash before any OOM kill.

alert.title: Elevated 5xx error rate on search-api
alert.description: 5xx at 22%, starting 3 minutes after deploy v4.9.0. All errors are 500s from one endpoint, /search/suggest, with "TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable". Dependencies are healthy.

notes: A code regression with a stack trace, isolated to one endpoint.

alert.title: Database write failures on billing-worker
alert.description: Writes fail with 'could not extend file: No space left on device'. The Postgres data volume is at 100%; the WAL directory grew by 60GB after a replication slot stopped being consumed.

notes: Presents as a database problem, but the mechanism is a full volume (WAL growth).

alert.title: Upstream timeouts on notifications-service
alert.description: Calls to the third-party SMS provider time out (p99 10s, the configured timeout). The provider's status page confirms degraded performance. CPU and memory are normal and there were no deploys this week.

notes: No runbook covers a slow third-party provider, so retrieval is not scored for this case.

alert.title: CrashLoopBackOff on reporting-api
alert.description: The container is killed by its liveness probe after 10s. Logs show the app is still loading its 2GB model file when killed (this normally takes ~25s); there are no errors before termination. The probe config is unchanged, but the model file doubled in size last week.

notes: A slow-but-healthy start killed by the liveness probe; the CrashLoopBackOff runbook covers this case explicitly.
